subject: Latency guardrails & reserved GPU sizing — post-demo checklist
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@finopt.ai>, Tom Riley <tom.riley@finopt.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Latency guardrails & reserved GPU sizing — post-demo checklist

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the candid Q&A. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the pilot: 

Summary of SLO asks from the call:
- Frontend UX: p95 end-to-end latency <= 120 ms (character-level streaming for autocomplete UI).
- Backend scoring: p99 <= 350 ms for single-turn batches (non-streaming).
- Sustained throughput: 100 req/s across peak window (10:00–11:00 PT), with burst tolerance up to 300 req/s for short spikes.
- Concurrent requests: expect bursts that require ~40 concurrent generation contexts per model shard during peak.
- Streaming: we need server-push (chunked responses) with connection hold times up to 8s for long generations.

Initial GPU options we discussed (for dedicated/reserved pilot):
- NVIDIA A100 80GB (preferred for larger KV-cache & long-context models).
- NVIDIA A100 40GB (cost-efficient for fp16 with moderate context lengths).
- H100 80GB (higher throughput for mixed-precision kernels but limited availability in our target region).

What we need from FinOpt to size the pilot:
1) Representative traffic sample (token lengths, request inter-arrival times) — replied and attached as "sherpa_perf_samples.csv".
2) Confirmation of strictest latency target (is p95 <= 120ms the hard requirement for all interactive flows?).
3) Any model variants you plan to use in prod (e.g., full-parameter model + quantized fallback).

Proposed Redwood deliverables for pilot (timeline below):
- Load profile mapping + recommended GPU shortlist by 11/30.
- Bench plan (concurrency, sustained rate, burst tests) and scripts by 12/01.
- Pilot window (reserved pool) proposal: 12/02–12/06 with acceptance criteria tied to p95/p99 and throughput.

Please reply with confirmations and the missing traffic sample if available. If the targets are different than above, flag them and we’ll re-run the sizing calc.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: demo_recording_20261126.mp3, sherpa_perf_samples.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency guardrails & reserved GPU sizing — post-demo checklist

Adding our internal test plan notes so we can move fast once FinOpt confirms traffic: 

Ben's bench priorities (short):
- Baseline: single-instance p95/p99 for the target model at nominal tokens (mean request = 120 tokens).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 10, 20, 40, 80 concurrent contexts to observe KV cache pressure and memory OOM thresholds.
- Sustained rate run: 100 req/s for 30 minutes to validate thermal & memory stability.
- Burst test: 300 req/s for 60 seconds repeated 3x to measure tail-latency and queueing behavior.
- Streaming test: chunked payload with simulated slow consumer to validate connection management (hold up to 8s).

Data/infra asks for bench:
- SDK keys and sandbox token access for scripted runs.
- Dataset sample (we can work off attached CSV) and expected tokenization rules.
- If they have any per-request pre/post-processing (rerankers, safety filters), we should include those to match real latency.

Tentative owner assignments:
- Ben: bench harness and result template (due 12/01).
- Karthik: HW selection + cost/perf trade spreadsheet (due 12/01).
- Marissa: procurement path + required order lead times for Reserved capacity (will confirm by 12/02).

I'll stand up a quick harness container and share the run commands.

-Ben

---
Note: internal only — do not send this note to FinOpt until we agree on test windows.

From: Elena Park <elena@finopt.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@finopt.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency guardrails & reserved GPU sizing — post-demo checklist

Thanks Dylan — this is great, and we appreciate the structured plan. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: the 120 ms p95 is for the primary autocomplete UI (client-facing). For backend batch scoring (internal pipelines) we can tolerate higher p99 up to 300–350 ms; good to see you captured that. Important: the UI path should also target tail behavior when token lengths increase — we will flag any requests > 300 tokens as "long-run" and those can be routed to a different pool if needed.

2) Traffic sample: attached is a small representative sample (columns: timestamp, tokens, user_tier). We'll follow up with a larger anonymized dump by COB Monday.

3) Model variants: we plan to run the full-parameter model in prod but would like an auto-fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant when latency spikes or capacity is constrained. Can Redwood support automatic fallback routing per policy (and do you have suggested rules)?

4) Resource regions & legal: we prefer capacity in the us-west-2 region and require that logs for the pilot are retained for 30 days. Any compliance-style metadata we should capture upfront?

We are comfortable with the proposed pilot window (12/02–12/06) as long as Redwood provides the bench harness and clear acceptance criteria. Tom and I will confirm the larger traffic dump Monday.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering | FinOpt.ai
Attachments: sherpa_perf_samples_small.csv

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency guardrails & reserved GPU sizing — post-demo checklist

Perfect — Elena, thanks for the clarifications and the sample. Noted the us-west-2 preference and 30-day log retention. We can absolutely implement model-fallback routing; Karthik will propose the exact policy (for example: p95 degradation threshold OR queueing depth > X triggers routing to quantized variant).

Immediate internal action items (owners + due dates):
- Karthik: produce GPU shortlist + fallback-routing policy draft (A100 80GB vs A100 40GB vs H100) + cost delta estimate for reserved window. Due: 2026-12-01 EOD.
- Ben: bench harness + run commands; share raw-run artifacts and result template. Due: 2026-12-01 EOD.
- Marissa: procurement checklist, estimated ordering lead times for reserved pool in us-west-2, and any SLA add-ons we should offer FinOpt. Due: 2026-12-02 EOD.
- Dylan: consolidate acceptance criteria doc and HubSpot activity. Due: 2026-11-30 EOD.

I'll attach the two small artifacts (demo recording and csv subset) to the HubSpot record and send a scheduling invite for a pre-pilot sync on 12/01 at 10am PT.

If anyone has constraints on the dates above speak up now; otherwise I'll proceed to confirm with FinOpt and set the pilot calendar.

Thanks,
Dylan
